newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish politician believed seized by separatists.
newsitem.headline: Spanish politician believed seized by separatists.

text.p: Spain has said a town councillor in the Basque region has disappeared and is assumed to have been kidnapped by ETA Basque separatists who have threatened to kill him in 48 hours.

A caller saying he was from ETA told a director at Basque radio Egin, ETA's usual mouthpiece, that Miguel Angel Blanco would be killed if the government did not move Basque prisoners nearer to their homeland. Blanco is a member of Spain's ruling Popular Party.
"We can confirm that Miguel Angel Blanco has disappeared," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told a news conference on Thursday after meeting Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar.
"We find ourselves faced with duress, a threat and blackmail, although this is not a simple challenge to the government, but a challenge to society," he said.
Blanco, a town councillor in Ermua, was last seen just after 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) on Thursday leaving his house to catch a train for work in the nearby town of Eibar, Mayor Oreja said.
Shortly afterwards, Egin received the call.

"There was a call by the terrorist band ETA to Egin communicating the kidnap of Blanco and saying if the government doesn't move all the ETA prisoners closer to the Basque region before Saturday at 4 p.m. they will assassinate him," Interior Ministry spokesman Cayetano Gonzalez said.

ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has been pushing the Popular Party government to move imprisoned members to jails in the Basque region. Under a long-standing policy, they are scattered around the country.
A Popular Party spokesman, Angel Acebes, said the government would stand firm on its policy toward the separatist guerrillas and would not bend to their demands.
"Once more the Popular Party reiterates that in ETA's actions of blackmail and terror there must be no distinctions in the way we treat different victims," he told a news conference.
The kidnapping poured cold water on the euphoria that followed the freeing of two ETA hostages last week.
"In the last few days we have shared moments of true happiness and today regrettably we must share moments of anxiety for the life of Miguel Angel," Mayor Oreja said.

Last week the separatists released kidnapped businessman Cosme Declaux after his family paid the captors $6.85 million, the largest ransom obtained by ETA, police sources said. Hours later, Spanish police rescued prison worker Jose Antonio Ortega Lara who had been held hostage by ETA for 532 days.
ETA, which has killed some 800 people in its nearly 30-year drive for Basque independence, had abducted the prison worker to pressure the government on its ETA prison policy.
Shortly after the two were freed, a spokesman from ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna said: "After the drunkenness comes the hangover."

"This kidnapping is a clear act of retaliation, it is an act of terrible cowardice and unjustifiable duress on the part of ETA and its political arm Herri Batasuna," Carlos Iturgaiz, president of the Popular Party in the Basque country, told reporters.

Egin alerted police on Thursday afternoon immediately after receiving the call in the name of ETA. An hour after the first call the same person called again, repeating the details of the kidnapping, authorities said.
Mayor Oreja said an office had been set up in the Basque region to coordinate the investigation.

"We desperately beg the authors of this last action that they do not act out their threat," Basque interior counsellor Juan Maria Atutxa told journalists. "I ask that these people listen to the outcry of these people that reject this hatred."
Blanco's mother, father and girlfriend sat at home anxiously awaiting news of the politician while hundreds of people marched through Ermua in protest at the kidnapping.
"This town councillor did not have an important role in the PP (Popular Party) and ETA probably took advantage of his lack of protection," said Carlos Totorika, mayor of Ermua.
Blanco is a trained economist who works as a consultant and has been a town councillor in Ermua for two years.
